html:
SMTO-EXE-0169 — SMTO won't add a spreadsheet formula that reaches outside the file

GUID: a04085af-222b-59e8-b034-aa395be392f5
Slug: office-external-link-blocked
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • The formula SMTO tried to add could link to another file, a website or a feature that can run outside the spreadsheet, so it was refused. The spreadsheet wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to rewrite the formula using plain cell ranges in this file, for example =SUM(B2:B10), instead of links to other files or table names in square brackets. Formulas that only use cells inside this spreadsheet are allowed.
  2. If you need a web address or link, ask SMTO to put it in the cell as plain text instead of using HYPERLINK or WEBSERVICE. Functions that can open websites or other programs are blocked to keep the spreadsheet safe.
  3. If you wanted the formula saved exactly as written and not as a working formula, ask SMTO to write it as text. Text is stored as-is and never runs.

What success looks like

  • SMTO saves the new spreadsheet with the allowed formula or text in the cell.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO if a formula that only uses this spreadsheet's cells is still refused. If you really need links to other files, add them yourself in your spreadsheet app.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Excel formula validation rejected the formula (office.external_link_blocked) because it contains external-workbook or structured-reference brackets, '|' (DDE), a URI or UNC path, or a blocked function (WEBSERVICE, HYPERLINK, RTD, DDE, CALL, REGISTER, EXEC or IMAGE); the formula was not executed.

What this means

  • Formula validation detected external-workbook/DDE/URI syntax or a conservatively blocked network/execution-capable function name. This syntax guard does not claim the formula was executed. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • Formula validation detected external-workbook/DDE/URI syntax or a conservatively blocked network/execution-capable function name. This syntax guard does not claim the formula was executed.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the requested formula form and whether it should instead be literal text or a supported local formula.

How to fix it

  • Supply a formula that references only cells in the same workbook, without [ ], |, ://, \ or the blocked functions, via excel_set_formula; or write the text as a literal with excel_write_range. Table structured references are blocked by this rule too and must use plain A1 ranges.
  • Use a local formula without external workbook, DDE, URI or network-function references, or write the string as literal data.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use a local formula without external workbook, DDE, URI or network-function references, or write the string as literal data.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberately chosen permitted formula is stored as data without calculation or external resolution.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
